Korean registry quantifies real-world lecanemab ARIA and early PET clearance

Among 663 lecanemab-treated patients at 32 Korean hospitals, ARIA occurred in 16.1%, symptomatic ARIA-E in 0.6%, and baseline superficial siderosis was associated with a 7.45-fold higher hazard of ARIA-E.

Key quantitative results: ARIA occurred in 106/657 patients (16.1%): ARIA-E with or without ARIA-H in 27 (4.1%) and isolated ARIA-H in 79 (12.0%). Four patients (0.6%) had symptomatic ARIA-E.

ManagementMRIARIA-EARIA-HTreatment safety monitoring

Added October 20, 2026 · DOI:10.1186/s13195-026-02232-z; JOY-ALZ registry

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The largest same-window real-world report provides actionable rates and risk associations for lecanemab safety. ARIA-E clustered with APOE ε4 homozygosity, worse baseline CDR-SB, microhemorrhages, and superficial siderosis. Clinician-selected dose titration reduced infusion reactions but did not show lower ARIA within genotype strata, so the observational data do not establish a safer off-label dosing strategy.

Study design

JOY-ALZ analyzed 663 patients with Alzheimer disease who received at least one lecanemab infusion across 32 hospitals. ARIA analyses included 657 patients with at least one monitoring MRI. Clinicians used dose titration selectively, and exploratory analyses related genotype, clinical status, baseline MRI markers, plasma p-tau217, and amyloid PET to safety and short-term outcomes.

Key quantitative results

  • ARIA occurred in 106/657 patients (16.1%): ARIA-E with or without ARIA-H in 27 (4.1%) and isolated ARIA-H in 79 (12.0%). Four patients (0.6%) had symptomatic ARIA-E.
  • ARIA-E was associated with APOE ε4 homozygosity (HR 2.81; 95% CI, 1.06–7.46), higher baseline CDR-SB (HR 1.18 per point; 95% CI, 1.04–1.35), more baseline microhemorrhages (HR 1.69; 95% CI, 1.32–2.16), and baseline superficial siderosis (HR 7.45; 95% CI, 1.50–37.12).
  • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 26.7% and were less frequent with dose titration, but ARIA-E and ARIA-H did not differ between standard and titration groups within APOE genotype strata.
  • MMSE declined by 0.15 points per month (95% CI, −0.21 to −0.08; p<0.001). Higher baseline plasma p-tau217 was associated with greater worsening in functional activities.
  • Amyloid PET became negative in 15/64 (23.4%) at 3–9 months and 8/29 (27.6%) at 10–12 months; lower baseline Centiloid (OR 0.92; 95% CI, 0.88–0.96) and higher baseline MMSE (OR 1.23; 95% CI, 1.04–1.45) were associated with negativity.

What changed

The multicenter registry supplies large-scale routine-care estimates for ARIA, infusion reactions, MRI risk factors, and early PET clearance under lecanemab outside a randomized trial.

Strength of evidence

Moderate real-world safety evidence from a large multicenter registry. Treatment, titration, MRI, and follow-up were not randomized; clinical and PET follow-up were short; and PET analyses involved small subsets, limiting efficacy and causal dosing conclusions.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Baseline superficial siderosis and microhemorrhage burden reinforced ARIA-E risk stratification, while symptomatic ARIA-E was uncommon. The data support careful label-based selection and MRI monitoring but do not justify changing dose or surveillance schedules.

Field medical relevance

Relevant to MSL discussions about real-world ARIA rates, APOE and MRI risk, dose titration, early PET response, and the difference between observational association and a validated monitoring strategy.

Quanterix or platform relevance

MRI markers were evaluated as ARIA-E risk factors, while small PET subsets were used to characterize early amyloid clearance. The study informs monitoring interpretation but does not validate an alternative MRI schedule, PET stopping rule, or p-tau217 response threshold.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No authorization, availability, reimbursement, or coverage change. The multicenter experience may inform implementation capacity but does not create a new access pathway.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Did dose titration reduce ARIA?
Not within APOE genotype strata. It was associated with fewer infusion reactions, but the nonrandomized analysis does not establish an ARIA-prevention effect.
Which baseline features were most strongly associated with ARIA-E?
Superficial siderosis had HR 7.45, APOE ε4 homozygosity HR 2.81, and each additional baseline microhemorrhage HR 1.69, with wide confidence intervals for some estimates.
Can early PET negativity guide stopping treatment?
No. PET data came from small observational subsets, and the study did not validate a stopping rule.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Observational registry without randomized dosing or comparator group
  • Clinician-selected dose titration creates confounding by indication
  • Short clinical follow-up
  • Small amyloid-PET follow-up subsets
  • Potential variation in routine-care imaging and outcome assessment
  • No validated treatment-stopping or biomarker-guided dosing rule
